teacher.model: Codex AI agent; requested gpt-6-astra; runtime not independently verified

examples.text: By Monday afternoon, I will put the invoice reconciliation sheet in your inbox.
examples.rationale: Direct author future delivery with a deadline and no condition.

examples.text: Our finance team commits to delivering the completed invoice reconciliation sheet tomorrow.
examples.rationale: Explicit unqualified team commitment to deliver a work item.

examples.text: I aim to put the invoice reconciliation sheet in your inbox by Monday afternoon.
examples.rationale: An aim is an intention, not an assured delivery.

examples.text: Please put the invoice reconciliation sheet in our inbox by Monday afternoon.
examples.rationale: Recipient request, not an author delivery assertion.

examples.text: Our support team will hand over the reproduction package before the troubleshooting call.
examples.rationale: Unqualified future delivery by the author team; the call marks a deadline.

examples.text: You will receive the reproduction package from me at nine tomorrow.
examples.rationale: Assured future recipient receipt with explicit author ownership.

examples.text: The customer quoted an earlier message: "Our support team will hand over the reproduction package tomorrow."
examples.rationale: A quoted earlier message is reported wording, not a new direct assertion.

examples.text: Our support team handed over the reproduction package before yesterday's troubleshooting call.
examples.rationale: Completed past delivery, not a prospective assertion.

examples.text: I promise to upload the localization glossary for you on Thursday.
examples.rationale: Explicit author promise of future work-item delivery.

examples.text: The localization glossary is going out from our team this evening.
examples.rationale: Definite scheduled delivery and explicit author-team origin.

examples.text: I will upload the localization glossary on Thursday if the translators sign it off.
examples.rationale: Future delivery depends on an explicit approval condition.

examples.text: Could your team upload the localization glossary for us on Thursday?
examples.rationale: Asks the recipient team to deliver; no author-owned delivery assertion.

examples.text: We are sending you the office-hours agenda first thing tomorrow.
examples.rationale: Scheduled future-progressive delivery by the author team.

examples.text: Before our office hours start, I will share the complete agenda with you.
examples.rationale: Direct unqualified author future sharing with a deadline.

examples.text: The account history says we promised to share an office-hours agenda before the session.
examples.rationale: Historical attribution of a promise rather than a fresh author assertion.

examples.text: We will not send an office-hours agenda before the session.
examples.rationale: Explicit negation of future delivery.

examples.text: I guarantee that our route-validation log will reach you by three tomorrow.
examples.rationale: Explicit guarantee of future delivery with author ownership.

examples.text: We will supply the route-validation log to your operations team this week.
examples.rationale: Unqualified author-team future supply of a concrete artifact.

examples.text: Our estimate is that the route-validation log will reach you by three tomorrow.
examples.rationale: Delivery timing is framed as an estimate, not an assurance.

examples.text: Will your operations team supply its route-validation log to us this week?
examples.rationale: Question requests the recipient team's delivery.

examples.text: The decommission runbook will be delivered by our team on Tuesday morning.
examples.rationale: Passive future delivery explicitly owned by the author team.

examples.text: I am going to hand you the final decommission runbook at our next meeting.
examples.rationale: Definite author-owned future handover of a work item.

examples.text: Jo told us that her team would deliver the decommission runbook on Tuesday morning.
examples.rationale: Reports another person's delivery statement.

examples.text: If we owned the decommission runbook, we would send it to you.
examples.rationale: Counterfactual delivery, not a firm real-world future assertion.

examples.text: We undertake to send you the service-credit calculation worksheet tomorrow.
examples.rationale: Explicit undertaking to deliver a document; no promise about the credit amount.

examples.text: Your service-credit calculation worksheet will come from me before noon on Wednesday.
examples.rationale: Unqualified future recipient receipt explicitly attributed to the author.

examples.text: Pending the billing review, we will send the service-credit calculation worksheet tomorrow.
examples.rationale: Delivery is conditional on an unfinished review.

examples.text: Would you send us the service-credit calculation worksheet before noon on Wednesday?
examples.rationale: Recipient request rather than an author-owned delivery statement.

examples.text: I will email you the consent wording draft this afternoon.
examples.rationale: Direct author future delivery of a draft; no claim that its contents are approved.

examples.text: We give you our word that the consent wording draft will be shared tomorrow.
examples.rationale: Explicit author-team assurance of future document delivery.

examples.text: The project diary records my previous promise to email a consent wording draft this afternoon.
examples.rationale: Historical record of a promise rather than a new unqualified assertion.

examples.text: The consent wording draft has already been emailed to your team.
examples.rationale: Completed delivery rather than a future one.

examples.text: We commit to providing the seat-allocation register at the end of this week.
examples.rationale: Explicit team commitment to future artifact delivery.

examples.text: I will make the completed seat-allocation register available to you tomorrow morning.
examples.rationale: Unqualified author future provision of the register.

examples.text: We expect to provide the seat-allocation register at the end of this week.
examples.rationale: Expectation is qualified delivery rather than a promise.

examples.text: Can you make the completed seat-allocation register available to us tomorrow morning?
examples.rationale: Requests recipient provision of the register.

examples.text: Our engineering team will send the load-test summary on Friday.
examples.rationale: Unqualified future delivery by the author team.

examples.text: I promise that you will have the load-test summary from us before the review begins.
examples.rationale: Explicit future-delivery assurance; the review marks a deadline.

examples.text: The forwarded note reads: "Our engineering team will send the load-test summary on Friday."
examples.rationale: Quoted forwarded text, not a fresh assertion by the current author.

examples.text: I cannot promise to send the load-test summary on Friday.
examples.rationale: Negates the act of promising; does not assure future delivery.
